rose.name: Rose
rose.habitat: Cultivated worldwide, especially in temperate regions. Thrives in well-drained soil and sunny locations.
rose.description: Used for skin care and in cosmetics. The petals have anti-inflammatory properties and are often used in face masks and lotions.
rose.precautions: Generally safe, but people with plant allergies should be cautious.

tulsi.name: Tulsi
tulsi.habitat: Native to the Indian subcontinent, grows in tropical and subtropical climates. Prefers sunny locations and well-drained soil.
tulsi.description: Used in Ayurveda for its medicinal properties. It is believed to enhance immunity and relieve stress.
tulsi.precautions: Avoid during pregnancy without consulting a healthcare provider. May lower blood sugar.

aloevera.name: Aloevera
aloevera.habitat: Native to the Arabian Peninsula, but cultivated worldwide. Thrives in arid and semi-arid regions with well-drained soil.
aloevera.description: Known for its soothing and healing properties. Often used to treat burns, cuts, and other skin issues.
medicinal_uses: Topical treatment for burns and cuts
aloevera.precautions: Do not consume the whole leaf; only use the inner gel. Oral consumption can have a laxative effect.

lavender.name: Lavender
lavender.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean region. Grows well in dry, sandy, or gravelly soils and prefers full sun.
lavender.description: Used in aromatherapy for relaxation and sleep improvement. The scent is known for its calming effects.
lavender.precautions: Undiluted essential oil can irritate the skin. Do not ingest essential oil.

jasmine.name: Jasmine
jasmine.habitat: Native to tropical and subtropical regions. Prefers well-drained soil and full sun to partial shade.
jasmine.description: Used in aromatherapy for its calming effects and to reduce stress. Jasmine flowers are also used in perfumes and teas.
jasmine.precautions: Generally safe. Pregnant women should consult a doctor before using jasmine oil.

hibiscus.name: Hibiscus
hibiscus.habitat: Native to tropical and subtropical regions. Thrives in warm climates with well-drained soil.
hibiscus.description: Rich in antioxidants and used to lower blood pressure. Hibiscus tea is a popular beverage known for its tart flavor.
hibiscus.precautions: Can significantly lower blood pressure. May interact with blood pressure medications.

echinacea.name: Echinacea
echinacea.habitat: Native to North America. Prefers well-drained soil and full sun.
echinacea.description: Boosts the immune system and is used to prevent colds. Echinacea is often used in herbal supplements and teas.
echinacea.precautions: People with autoimmune disorders should consult a doctor. Short-term use is recommended.

banana.name: Banana
banana.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia, now grown worldwide in tropical climates. Requires warm temperatures and moist, fertile soil.
banana.description: Rich in potassium and dietary fiber. Used as an energy source and for digestive health.
banana.precautions: People with a latex allergy may have a cross-reaction to bananas.

bilimbi.name: Bilimbi
bilimbi.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Prefers warm, humid climates and well-drained soil.
bilimbi.description: Fruit is sour and used in traditional medicine to lower cholesterol and control hypertension.
bilimbi.precautions: High in oxalic acid, so consume in moderation, especially if you have kidney issues.

cantaloupe.name: Cantaloupe
cantaloupe.habitat: Cultivated in warm regions worldwide. Prefers sandy loam soil and full sunlight.
cantaloupe.description: Rich in vitamin C and antioxidants. Helps with hydration and immune support.
cantaloupe.precautions: Generally safe. Wash the rind thoroughly before cutting to avoid bacterial contamination.

cassava.name: Cassava
cassava.habitat: Native to South America, widely cultivated in tropical regions. Grows in poor, sandy soils.
cassava.description: Staple root crop rich in carbohydrates. Used to make flour, tapioca, and traditional foods.
cassava.precautions: Must be properly peeled and cooked to remove cyanide compounds. Never eat raw.

coconut.name: Coconut
coconut.habitat: Tropical coastal regions worldwide. Requires sandy soil and high humidity.
coconut.description: Fruit provides water, milk, oil, and fiber. Used in food, cosmetics, and medicine.
coconut.precautions: High in saturated fat, so consume oil in moderation.

corn.name: Corn
corn.habitat: Native to the Americas, cultivated globally. Grows well in warm climates and fertile soil.
corn.description: Staple cereal crop rich in carbohydrates. Used as food, livestock feed, and biofuel.
corn.precautions: Generally safe. Can be difficult to digest for some people.

cucumber.name: Cucumber
cucumber.habitat: Native to South Asia, cultivated worldwide. Prefers warm climates with moist soil.
cucumber.description: High in water content, promotes hydration and skin health. Commonly eaten fresh or pickled.
cucumber.precautions: Generally safe. People with a pollen-food allergy syndrome may have a reaction.

curcuma.name: Curcuma
curcuma.habitat: Native to tropical South Asia. Thrives in warm, humid regions with fertile soil.
curcuma.description: Includes turmeric species, used for anti-inflammatory and antioxidant purposes.
curcuma.precautions: Can act as a blood thinner. Avoid if you have gallbladder problems or are pregnant.

eggplant.name: Eggplant
eggplant.habitat: Native to Asia, cultivated globally. Prefers warm climates with well-drained soil.
eggplant.description: Rich in fiber, antioxidants, and vitamins. Used in various cuisines worldwide.
eggplant.precautions: People with nightshade sensitivity may have a reaction. Avoid eating raw.

galangal.name: Galangal
galangal.habitat: Native to Southeast Asia. Thrives in tropical climates with moist, fertile soil.
galangal.description: Used in Asian cuisine and traditional medicine. Believed to improve digestion and reduce inflammation.
galangal.precautions: Generally safe in culinary amounts. Medicinal doses should be discussed with a doctor.

guava.name: Guava
guava.habitat: Native to Central America, now cultivated in tropical regions worldwide. Adaptable to various soils.
guava.description: A tropical fruit rich in vitamin C, antioxidants, and dietary fiber. Commonly eaten fresh or used in juices and preserves.
guava.precautions: Excessive consumption may cause bloating in some individuals.

kale.name: Kale
kale.habitat: Native to the Mediterranean. Thrives in cool climates with moist, fertile soil.
kale.description: Leafy green superfood high in vitamins A, C, and K, along with antioxidants and fiber.
kale.precautions: High in vitamin K, which may interfere with blood-thinning medications. People with thyroid issues should consume in moderation.

longbeans.name: Long Beans
longbeans.habitat: Native to Africa, widely cultivated in Asia. Prefers warm climates with well-drained soil.
longbeans.description: A climbing legume rich in fiber, protein, and vitamins. Popular in Asian cuisine.
longbeans.precautions: Generally safe. Best consumed cooked for easier digestion.

mango.name: Mango
mango.habitat: Native to South Asia. Grows best in tropical and subtropical climates.
mango.description: A sweet tropical fruit high in vitamins A and C, fiber, and antioxidants. Widely enjoyed fresh or in drinks.
mango.precautions: Mango peel may cause allergic reactions in people sensitive to poison ivy, oak, or sumac.
